skipped.reason: no card in Forge has more than one fortify ability, so the rule cannot be illustrated; activating a fortify ability is covered by 702.67a-1

scenarios.title: Fortify attaches the Fortification to the target land when the ability resolves
decisions: A activates the fortify ability of Darksteel Garrison targeting Evolving Wilds, tapping three Mountains for {3}.
Both players pass priority; the ability resolves.

variants.label: target_stays_legal
variants.expected: The fortify ability resolves. Darksteel Garrison is attached to Evolving Wilds, which has indestructible. No cards change zones.

variants.label: target_leaves_in_response
variants.delta: After the fortify ability is on the stack, A taps and sacrifices Evolving Wilds (fetching a Forest from the library) before passing priority.
variants.expected: The fortify ability fizzles because its only target is gone. Darksteel Garrison stays on the battlefield unattached. Evolving Wilds is in A's graveyard and A's Forest enters tapped.

scenarios.title: Fortify may be activated only as a sorcery and only targets a land its controller controls
decisions: Evaluate whether A may activate the fortify ability of Darksteel Garrison, and which lands are legal targets, with the stack empty and four untapped Mountains.

variants.label: main_phase
variants.expected: The activation is legal (can_play true). The legal targets are A's four Mountains; B's Forest is not a legal target.

variants.label: during_combat
variants.delta: The step is declare_attackers instead of main1.
variants.expected: The activation is not legal (can_play false), because fortify may be activated only as a sorcery.
